mainTopic: Dividing shared money, renting out coins, and when extra payment around a loan or rental counts as רבית
overview: The amud opens by finishing a story about רב פפא. He explains to a litigant that coins may be split without the partner present, but wine may not, because wine varies in quality. The גמרא then limits רב נחמן's rule that money counts as already divided: it applies only when all the coins are the same kind. Next comes the story of רב חמא, who 'rented out' coins for a daily fee. The גמרא explains that coins are not like a rented hoe, so this is really a loan with רבית. רבא and רב פפא then teach that the Torah forbids only interest paid from the borrower to the lender, so a fee paid to a middleman is allowed. A new משנה allows giving an animal to someone to raise for half the profit. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows raising the rent on a field, and the גמרא explains when a field, store or ship may get higher rent in exchange for money to improve it. Finally, רב allows renting a ship for both rent and payment for damage. רב ששת defends this with a ברייתא about a cow, and רב פפא rules like רב.

steps.title: In a case like this, the judge must explain
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says that in this kind of case he certainly has to tell the litigant the reason for his ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a case like this, it is certainly necessary to let him know the reason.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא decides that he must explain his ruling to the litigant. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a judge does not have to give reasons for his ruling. Here the litigant could suspect unfairness, since last year a split of money was allowed without him. So רב פפא chooses to explain the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: to let him know, to inform him

phrases.english: In a case like this it is certainly necessary to inform him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is the litigant who lost the case. רב פפא feels he owes him the reason.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּהַאי גַּוְנָא וַדַּאי צְרִיךְ לְאוֹדוֹעֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from the previous section, where the litigant asked why he lost.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a ruling looks unfair compared with an earlier one, the judge should explain his reasoning.

steps.title: Did the other partner pick the good coins?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks the litigant whether, when the money was split last year, the other side took the good coins and left the worn ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: With the coins, did he take the good ones and leave the worn ones?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא begins his explanation by asking the litigant a question about last year's split of money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is meant to show that coins are all basically equal. If no one picks the 'better' coins, splitting them without the partner present cheats nobody.

phrases.english: The coins, did he take the good ones
and leave the deficient ones?

steps.triggerLanguage: זוּזֵי, מִי שָׁקֵיל טָבֵי וְשָׁבֵיק חַסִּרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the explanation promised in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the earlier split of money gave one side an advantage.

steps.title: The litigant says no
steps.stepSummary: The litigant admits that the other side did not choose the better coins.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: No.
steps.whatsHappening: The litigant answers that no, nobody picked the good coins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By saying this, the litigant admits that splitting the coins was fair. That gives רב פפא what he needs to contrast money with wine.

phrases.english: He said to him: No.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The split of money was even; no one gained.

steps.title: Wine is different because quality varies
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that everyone knows some wine is sweet and some is not, so wine cannot be split without the partner.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: With wine, everyone knows that some is sweet and some is not sweet.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the real reason for his ruling: wine is not all the same quality.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Coins are interchangeable, so one partner may divide them alone. Wine barrels differ in taste, so whoever divides alone could keep the better barrels. That is why the litigant had no right to split the wine by himself.
steps.whatToRemember: Money can be split by one partner alone because all coins are equal; wine cannot, because its quality varies.

phrases.english: He said to him: Wine,
everyone knows that there is some that is sweet
and there is some that is not sweet.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חַמְרָא, כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא יָדְעִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the litigant's answer to draw the contrast between money and wine.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A partner may not split wine without the other partner, because its quality varies.

steps.title: רב נחמן: money counts as already divided
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to רב נחמן's rule that shared money is treated as if it were already divided.
steps.simpleTranslation: Returning to the main point: רב נחמן said: Money is treated as if it were already divided.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to look closely at רב נחמן's rule, which it quoted earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since all coins are basically equal, each partner's share is already clear. So one partner may take his half without the other being present.

keyTerms.meaning: they are as if already divided

phrases.english: The matter itself: Rav Naḥman said:
Coins are considered as if they were divided.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story and returns to the rule behind it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Shared money may be split by one partner alone, since it counts as already divided.

steps.title: Only when the coins are all the same kind
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits רב נחמן's rule: it works only when all the coins are the same type, not a mix of good and heavy coins.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies to good coins with good coins, or heavy coins with heavy coins. But good coins mixed with heavy coins, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows רב נחמן's rule so it does not apply to a mix of coin types.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If all the coins are the same kind, nobody gains by choosing. If there are two kinds, a partner might prefer one kind. So he may not divide them alone.
steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן's rule works only when the coins are all the same kind.

phrases.english: This applies to good ones with good ones,
phrases.notes: "Good" and "heavy" are two different kinds of coins. Some people might prefer one kind over the other.

phrases.english: heavy ones with heavy ones.
But good ones with heavy ones, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי טָבֵי וְטָבֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule just quoted in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Money counts as divided only when all the coins are the same type.

steps.title: רב חמא rented out coins and lost his money
steps.stepSummary: רב חמא charged a daily fee for 'renting' coins and ended up losing all his money. He thought coins were no different from a rented hoe.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חמא would rent out coins for a פשיטא a day. רב חמא's money was all lost. He thought: How is this different from renting out a hoe?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a story about רב חמא, who treated lending coins like renting out a tool.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חמא thought a daily fee for coins was rent, not ריבית, just like charging rent for a hoe. His losing all his money hints that he was wrong. The next step explains why.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥama would rent out coins
for a peshita a day.
phrases.notes: A פשיטא is a small coin, an eighth of a זוז.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥama's money was lost.
He thought: How is it different from a hoe?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חָמָא הֲוָה מוֹגַר זוּזֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: renting out money.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב חמא treated renting coins like renting a tool, and he lost his money.

steps.title: Coins are not like a hoe
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב חמא's comparison. A hoe comes back itself and its wear can be seen; coins are spent and replaced, and their wear cannot be known.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is not so. A hoe comes back as it is, and its wear is known. Coins do not come back as they are, and their wear is not known.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows why רב חמא's reasoning was wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rent works when the same item comes back and the owner is paid for its visible wear. With coins, the borrower spends them and returns different ones, so nothing was really 'rented'. It is a loan, and the daily fee is ריבית.

keyTerms.meaning: as it is, the same item
its loss in value, its wear

steps.whatToRemember: Charging a fee to 'rent' money is really ריבית, because the same coins never come back.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think renting money is like renting a tool. With a tool, the same item comes back. With money, different coins come back, so it is a loan.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that you cannot get around the ban on ריבית by calling a loan of money 'rent'.

phrases.english: But it is not so:
a hoe returns as it is, and its depreciation is known;
coins do not return as they are,
and their depreciation is not known.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison רב חמא made in step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects comparing rented money to a rented tool.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A hoe comes back itself with visible wear; coins are spent and replaced, so the 'rent' is really ריבית on a loan.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Renting out money for a fee is a loan with ריבית.

steps.title: Paying someone to lend money to a third person
steps.stepSummary: רבא permits paying a person four זוזים to lend money to someone else, because the Torah forbids only interest that goes from the borrower to the lender.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A person may say to his friend, 'Here are four זוזים; now lend money to so-and-so.' The Torah forbade only interest that passes from the borrower to the lender.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new rule. You may pay someone to lend money to a different person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The friend who lends does gain from the loan. But the money he gains does not come from the borrower. It comes from an outside person. רבא says the Torah's ban on רבית covers only payment that passes directly from the borrower to the lender.

keyTerms.meaning: Interest, which the Torah forbids on loans

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the key line for the rest of the section: what is forbidden is payment from the borrower to the lender.

phrases.english: Rava said:
It is permitted for a person
to say to his friend:
Here are four zuz for you
and lend money to so-and-so.
The Torah forbade only
interest that comes from the borrower to the lender.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: שְׁרֵי לֵיהּ לְאִינִישׁ לְמֵימַר לֵיהּ לְחַבְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the rented-coins discussion to a new set of rulings about interest that involves a third person.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Paying a lender to lend to someone else is permitted, because the Torah forbids only interest from borrower to lender.

steps.title: The borrower pays a middleman to arrange his loan
steps.stepSummary: רבא permits a borrower to pay someone four זוזים to ask a lender to lend him money, because this is payment for speaking.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא also said: A person may say to his friend, 'Take four זוזים for yourself, and tell so-and-so to lend me money.' Why is this allowed? Because the friend is being paid for speaking.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second ruling, which is the flip side of the first. Here the borrower himself pays, but he pays the middleman, not the lender.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the money does come from the borrower. But it goes to the person who asks for the loan, not to the person who gives it. So it is a fee for a service, not interest.

keyTerms.meaning: Payment for speaking, a broker's fee

steps.confusionAlert: In this ruling the payer is the borrower. It is allowed only because the money goes to the middleman and not to the lender.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
It is permitted for a person
to say to his friend:
"Take four zuz for yourself
and tell so-and-so
to lend me money."
What is the reason?
He is taking payment for speaking.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: שְׁרֵי לֵיהּ לְאִינִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ruling by רבא that fits with the first: here the borrower pays a middleman.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A borrower may pay a middleman to arrange a loan, since that is a fee for speaking and not interest.

steps.title: The story of אבא מר and the wax pans
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a real case: אבא מר, son of רב פפא, took wax from wax makers and asked his father to lend them money.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like the case of אבא מר, son of רב פפא. He used to take pans of wax from the wax makers, and then tell his father, 'Lend them money.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real-life case that matches רבא's second ruling. It is setting up the objection that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wax makers were the borrowers. They gave wax to the son, who acted as a middleman. The father was the lender and received nothing extra.

phrases.english: Like this case
where Abba Mar, son of Rav Pappa,
would take pans of wax from the wax makers,
and say to his father:
Lend them money.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּאַבָּא מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real case that supports רבא's 'payment for speaking' rule.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's rule that a middleman may be paid for arranging a loan
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of אבא מר, son of רב פפא, and how רב פפא defended it

steps.title: The רבנן object: your son is taking interest
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן tell רב פפא that his son is eating interest.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said to רב פפא: Your son is eating interest!
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן challenge the practice. They see the wax as payment for the loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wax came from the borrowers because of a loan from the family. So it looked to them like forbidden רבית.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master's son, a respectful way of saying 'your son'

phrases.english: The Sages said to Rav Pappa:
The Master's son is eating interest!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case just described.
steps.kashyaTarget: אבא מר's practice of taking wax from the borrowers
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wax is a gain that comes from the borrowers because of a loan, so it looks like רבית.

steps.title: רב פפא: this kind of interest is fine
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the Torah forbids only interest from borrower to lender. His son is only being paid for speaking.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: We may eat all interest like this! The Torah forbade only interest that comes from the borrower to the lender. Here, he is taking payment for speaking, and that is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the רבנן using the same two ideas רבא gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two points work together here. First, nothing reached the lender, who was the father. Second, the son earned the wax as a fee for asking his father. So it is not forbidden רבית at all.

keyTerms.meaning: We may eat, meaning we may benefit

steps.whatToRemember: Forbidden רבית means payment from the borrower to the lender. Money paid by an outsider to the lender, or paid by the borrower to a middleman for arranging the loan, is permitted.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: כֹּל כִּי הַאי רִבִּיתָא נֵיכוֹל,
phrases.english: He said to them: We may eat all interest like this!
The Torah forbade only
interest that comes from the borrower to the lender.
Here, he is taking payment for speaking,
phrases.notes: The son was paid for asking his father to lend. The father, who was the actual lender, got nothing.

phrases.english: and it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: כֹּל כִּי הַאי רִבִּיתָא נֵיכוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the רבנן's objection.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: the payment is a broker's fee and never reaches the lender.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any gain that comes from the borrowers because of a loan is forbidden רבית.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only payment from the borrower to the lender is forbidden. A fee for speaking is permitted.

steps.title: משנה: raising someone else's working animal for half the profit
steps.stepSummary: The משנה allows valuing a cow, a donkey, or any animal that works for its food, and giving it to someone to raise for half the profit. Local custom decides when the offspring are divided.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may value a cow, a donkey, or anything that works and eats, and give it out for half the profit. Where the custom is to divide the offspring right away, they divide them. Where the custom is to raise them first, they raise them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It allows a deal where the owner gives an animal to someone to care for, and they share the profit equally.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animal's work pays for the caretaker's effort in feeding it. So the caretaker is not working for free, and the owner's share of the profit does not look like interest. When to divide the offspring is decided by local custom.

keyTerms.meaning: They value, setting a price on an animal
Works and eats, meaning it earns its own food

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One may value a cow and a donkey
and anything that works and eats
and give it out for half the profit.
In a place where the custom is to divide
the offspring right away, they divide them.
In a place where the custom is to raise them, they raise them.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ שָׁמִין פָּרָה וַחֲמוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה on profit-sharing deals involving animals.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal that earns its keep may be given out to be raised for half the profit. Local custom decides when the offspring are divided.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: young animals with their mothers, and raising the field rent
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows valuing a calf or foal together with its mother, and allows raising the rent on a field, without worrying about interest.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: One may value a calf together with its mother, and a foal together with its mother. And one may raise the rent on his field, and need not worry about interest.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds more lenient rulings to the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A calf or foal does not work for its food, but he allows it when it goes along with its working mother. He also allows charging a higher rent for a field, and the גמרא will explain why this is not רבית.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who disagrees with the first opinion in this משנה

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
One may value a calf together with its mother,
and a foal together with its mother,
and one may raise the rent on his field,
and he need not worry about interest.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: שָׁמִין עֵגֶל עִם אִמּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a more lenient view on the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A young animal may be valued along with its mother, and a field's rent may be raised, without a problem of רבית.

steps.title: A renter may raise the rent on a field in exchange for money to improve it
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains the earlier rule about raising the rent on a field. A renter borrows 200 זוז from the owner to improve the field and pays 12 כור a year instead of 10. This is מותר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא: The רבנן taught: A person may raise the rent on his field and not worry about רבית. How? Someone rents a field from his friend for ten כור of wheat a year. He tells the owner: 'Give me two hundred זוז and I will improve the field, and I will pay you twelve כור a year.' This is מותר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by quoting a ברייתא that explains the משנה's rule about raising the rent on a field. It gives an exact example of how this works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner gives the renter money, and the renter pays more rent. This looks like a loan with extra payment. But the money goes into the field itself, so the owner is getting higher rent for a better field, not payment for lending money.

keyTerms.meaning: And I will take care of it (improve the field)

steps.confusionAlert: The 200 זוז still has to be paid back. The extra 2 כור is allowed only because it counts as rent for an improved field, not as a fee for the loan.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:
One may raise the rent on his field
and he need not worry about interest. How so?
One who rents a field from his friend
for ten kor of wheat a year,

phrases.aramaic: וְאוֹמֵר לוֹ: תֵּן לִי מָאתַיִם זוּז
phrases.english: and says to him: Give me two hundred zuz
and I will take care of it,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲנִי אַעֲלֶה לְךָ שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר כּוֹרִין לְשָׁנָה – מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: and I will pay you twelve kor a year – it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַפְרִיז עַל שָׂדֵהוּ וְאֵינוֹ חוֹשֵׁשׁ מִשּׁוּם רִבִּית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the משנה's ruling (Step 15) that a person may raise the rent on a field.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Borrowing money from the owner to improve a rented field in exchange for higher rent is allowed.

steps.title: The same deal is not allowed for a store or a ship
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: a renter may not get money from the owner in exchange for higher rent on a store or a ship.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a person may not raise the rent on a store or on a ship.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא sets a limit on the field rule. The higher-rent deal does not work for a store or a ship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a store or ship, the borrowed money would usually buy merchandise, not improve the property. So the extra rent is really payment for the loan, which is רבית.

phrases.english: But one may not raise the rent

phrases.aramaic: לֹא עַל חֲנוּת וְלֹא עַל סְפִינָה.
phrases.english: neither on a store nor on a ship.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל אֵין מַפְרִיז לֹא עַל חֲנוּת וְלֹא עַל סְפִינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and limits its permission to fields.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Raising the rent in exchange for a loan is forbidden for a store or a ship.

steps.title: Sometimes a store or ship may also get a higher rent
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, says there are cases where a store or ship may get a higher rent: painting a design on a store, or making a sail for a ship.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: There are times when a person may raise the rent on a store, to paint a design on it, and on a ship, to make a sail for it.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא narrows the ברייתא's ban. He gives cases where even a store or ship can get the higher-rent deal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא banned stores and ships in general. רב נחמן says this is not a total ban: if the money goes into the property itself, it is like the field case and is allowed.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
There are times when one may raise the rent on a store
to paint a design on it,
and on a ship, to make a sail for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ: פְּעָמִים שֶׁמַּפְרִיז עַל חֲנוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the ban in Step 17 by giving exceptions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A store or ship may get a higher rent when the money is used to improve the property itself.

steps.title: Why painting a store or making a sail counts as improving the property
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains: a painted store draws more customers, and a nicer sail makes the ship earn more. So the money truly improves the property, like the field.
steps.simpleTranslation: A store, to paint a design on it: because people are drawn to it, and the profit is greater. A ship, to make a sail for it: since the sail is nicer, the profit is greater.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains each of רב נחמן's two examples. It shows how the money makes the property itself earn more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is whether the money makes the rented property more valuable. A painted store attracts buyers, and a better sail improves the ship. So the higher rent is paid for a better property, not for the loan.
steps.whatToRemember: Higher rent in exchange for the owner's money is allowed only when the money improves the rented property itself: a field, a painted store, or a new sail.

phrases.english: A store, to paint a design on it:
because people are drawn to it
and the profit becomes greater.
A ship, to make a sail for it:
since the sail is nicer,
the profit is greater.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲנוּת לָצוֹר בָּהּ צוּרְתָּא: דְּצָבוּ בַּהּ אִינָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the two exceptions in Step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These improvements raise the property's earnings, so the higher rent is fair rent and not רבית.

steps.title: רב: A ship may be rented for rent plus payment for damage
steps.stepSummary: Since the topic is ships, the גמרא brings רב's ruling: a ship may be rented so that the renter pays rent and is also responsible for damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: About a ship, רב said: rent and damage.
steps.whatsHappening: The topic of ships leads the גמרא to a new ruling from רב. It opens a new short discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב allows a ship deal where the renter pays rent and also covers any damage to the ship. This sets up the challenge in the next step.

phrases.english: About a ship, Rav said:
rent and damage.
phrases.notes: This is a short way of saying the owner can collect rent and also get paid for any damage to the ship.

steps.triggerLanguage: סְפִינְתָּא, אָמַר רַב: אַגְרָא וּפַגְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ship example in Step 18 to a separate ship ruling of רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An owner may rent out a ship and charge both rent and responsibility for damage.

steps.title: רב כהנא and רב אסי: You cannot charge both rent and damage
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא and רב אסי challenge רב: if it is a rental, the renter should not pay for damage; if he pays for damage, he should not pay rent.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא and רב אסי said to רב: If rent, then not damage. If damage, then not rent.
steps.whatsHappening: Two students attack רב's ruling. They say the two payments cannot go together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A renter normally does not carry full responsibility for damage. If the renter carries full responsibility, the ship is treated like a loan to him. Then the rent is extra payment for a loan, which is רבית.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ רַב כָּהֲנָא וְרַב אַסִּי לְרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Kahana and Rav Asi said to Rav:
If rent – then not damage,
if damage – then not rent.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אַגְרָא – לָא פַּגְרָא, אִי פַּגְרָא – לָא אַגְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רב's ruling in Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that a ship may be rented for both rent and damage.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Full responsibility for damage turns the deal into a loan. Charging rent on a loan is רבית, so the owner must pick one: rent or damage.

steps.title: רב stays silent
steps.stepSummary: רב does not answer the challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב was silent.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives no answer to his students' challenge. The next step asks why he stayed silent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's silence makes it look as if he had no answer to their challenge. The next step shows that a ברייתא could have backed him up, and step 26 rules like רב.

phrases.english: Rav was silent.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁתֵיק רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the challenge from Step 21 with no answer from רב.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב does not answer the challenge himself. רב ששת supplies the answer in the next step.

steps.title: רב ששת brings a ברייתא that supports רב
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת asks why רב stayed silent, since a ברייתא supports him. The ברייתא allows renting out a cow at a fixed value plus monthly rent.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: Why was רב silent? Hadn't he heard the ברייתא? It teaches: even though the Sages said you may not take 'iron sheep' from a Jew, though you may take them from gentiles, they did say this: if a man has a cow valued for his friend, and the friend says, 'Your cow is counted on me at thirty dinars, and I will pay you a sela every month,' it is permitted, because he did not turn it into a money loan.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת steps in to defend רב. He says רב could have answered the challenge by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key part of the ברייתא is the cow case. The renter takes responsibility for the cow's value and also pays monthly rent, and this is allowed. That is exactly what רב allowed for a ship: rent plus responsibility for damage.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Iron sheep': a deal where the receiver fully guarantees the animals' value but the owner still shares the profit. This counts as forbidden interest between Jews.
One who sets a money value on a cow
A coin; here it is the monthly rent payment
He turned it into money, meaning he treated it as a loan

steps.confusionAlert: The first part of the ברייתא, about צאן ברזל and gentiles, is only background. The proof for רב comes from the cow case after the words אבל אמרו.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רב's silence did not mean he had no answer. A ברייתא supports his ruling.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
What is the reason that Rav was silent?
phrases.notes: This is the silence from the last step, when רב did not answer רב כהנא and רב אסי.

phrases.english: Did he not hear that which is taught in a ברייתא:
Even though the Sages said
that one may not accept 'iron sheep' from a Jew,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מְקַבְּלִין צֹאן בַּרְזֶל מִן הַגּוֹיִם.
phrases.english: but one may accept 'iron sheep' from gentiles.
Nevertheless, they said:
If one sets a value on a cow for his friend,
and the friend said to him:

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי פָּרָתְךָ עֲשׂוּיָה עָלַי בִּשְׁלֹשִׁים דִּינָר,
phrases.english: Your cow is counted on me at thirty dinars,
and I will pay you a sela each month
it is permitted,
because he did not turn it into money.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב ששת: מאי טעמא שתיק רב? לא שמיעא ליה הא דתניא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge that רב left unanswered in step 22.
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that a ship may be rented for both rent and responsibility for damage (step 20).
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: a cow counted at thirty dinars on the receiver, plus a sela of rent each month, is permitted.

steps.title: But he did make it a loan
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the cow deal is not a loan, since the receiver took on its value of thirty dinars.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he did not make it into money?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's reason. The receiver did promise thirty dinars, so it looks like a loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the receiver owes thirty dinars no matter what, the cow is really a loan of thirty dinars. Then the monthly sela looks like interest. This is the same attack רב כהנא and רב אסי made against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he did not make it so?!' A surprised challenge

phrases.english: And did he not make it into money?!

steps.triggerLanguage: ולא עשאה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason given in the ברייתא brought in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that the receiver 'did not make it into money'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Promising a fixed value of thirty dinars turns the cow into a loan, so the monthly rent should be interest.

steps.title: The fixed value applies only if the cow dies
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that the thirty dinars is owed only if the cow dies. While the cow is alive, its loss in value is the owner's.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: He did not make it into money while it is alive, only after it dies.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the challenge by explaining what the ברייתא means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the cow gets old or thin, the owner takes that loss, so the cow still belongs to the owner. The renter pays thirty dinars only if the cow dies. So this is a real rental with added responsibility, not a loan, and the monthly sela is rent, not interest.
steps.whatToRemember: A renter may take responsibility for the item and still pay rent. This works as long as the owner keeps ownership, including normal loss in value.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
He did not make it into money while it is alive,
but only after its death.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב ששת: לא עשאה דמים מחיים, אלא לאחר מיתה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the receiver's responsibility applies only to the cow's death.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The receiver owes thirty dinars no matter what, which makes the deal a loan.
steps.terutzMaskana: The receiver owes only if the cow dies. The owner still owns the cow, so the monthly payment is real rent.

steps.title: The הלכה: a ship may be rented for rent and damage
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules like רב: when renting out a ship, one may collect rent and also make the renter pay for damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The הלכה is that with a ship, one may take rent and payment for damage.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the final ruling, and it follows רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because of the ברייתא about the cow, רב's ruling holds against the challenge of רב כהנא and רב אסי. Renting out a ship for both rent and responsibility is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'a carcass'; here it means payment for damage or loss

steps.whatToRemember: רב ששת defended רב's silence with the cow ברייתא, and רב פפא ruled like רב: a ship may be rented for both rent and payment for damage.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: The הלכה is:
A ship: rent and payment for damage.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב פפא, הלכתא: ספינה אגרא ופגרא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final ruling, following רב and the ברייתא as explained by רב ששת.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A ship may be rented so that the renter pays rent and also pays for damage.
